Lithium (from Ancient Greek: λίθος, líthos, 'stone') is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.

Pope Benedict XVI: Following his resignation, he chose to be known as "pope emeritus", a title he held until his death on 31 December 2022.
In what year was Iodine discovered?
Iodine is a chemical element; it has symbol I and atomic number 53.
In what year was Nickel discovered?
Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.
Magnesium sulfate: Pfizer. It is a white crystalline solid, soluble in water.
In which country is Fish and chips?
Fish and chips: United Kingdom. Fish and chips is a hot dish consisting of battered and fried fish, served with chips.
Who is credited with discovering Norma?

Norma (constellation): Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Its name is Latin for normal, referring to a right angle, and is variously considered to represent a rule, a carpenter's square, a set square or a level.
Who is credited with discovering Aspartame?
Aspartame: James M. Schlatter. Aspartame is an artificial, non-saccharide sweetener commonly used as a sugar substitute in foods and beverages.
Who is credited with discovering Histamine?
Histamine: Henry Hallett Dale. Histamine or histamin is an organic nitrogenous compound found in mammals and many vegetables, fruits and food products.
About 5 million tonnes of acetic acid are produced annually largely to make this compound, most commonly in polymer form — what is it?
Acetate is a salt formed by the combination of acetic acid with a base (e.g. sodium hydroxide), an ester of acetic acid, or the anion CH3COO- found in solution.
First described by Othniel C. Marsh in 1877, this late Jurassic theropod's name means 'different lizard,' a nod to its unusually lightweight vertebrae — what dinosaur is it?
Allosaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived 155 to 143 million years ago during the late Jurassic period (latest Oxfordian to latest Tithonian ages).
These eusocial insects evolved from vespoid wasps back in the Cretaceous, and you can spot one by its elbowed antennae and pinched, node-like waist. Which creature is it?
Ant are eusocial insects of the family Formicidae and, along with the related wasps and bees, belong to the order Hymenoptera.
Doctors reach for this NSAID not just for aches but to treat Kawasaki disease and rheumatic fever — and it's famous for its blood-thinning effect on platelets. What is it?
Aspirin is the genericized trademark for acetylsalicylic acid (ASA), a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to reduce pain, fever, and inflammation, and as an antithrombotic.
Ranging from 1 to 5 meters tall and found across Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas, this shrub genus's best-known species is the European type also called barberry — what genus is it?
Berberis is a large genus of deciduous and evergreen shrubs from 1-5 m (3+12-16+12 ft) tall, found throughout temperate and subtropical regions of the world (apart from Australia).
Every subatomic particle is either this integer-spin class or a fermion; Paul Dirac named the class after physicist Satyendra Nath Bose, whose statistics they obey — what's the class called?
Boson is a subatomic particle whose spin quantum number has an integer value (0, 1, 2,...).
With the chemical formula CaO, this white, caustic, alkaline solid is produced by heating limestone and has been used since antiquity in construction and agriculture — what's the compound's name?
Calcium oxide (formula: CaO), commonly known as quicklime or burnt lime, is a widely used chemical compound.
Sporting one pair of legs per body segment, this venomous arthropod always has an odd number of leg pairs — anywhere from 15 to 191 — what is it?

Centipede (from Neo-Latin centi- 'hundred' and Latin pes, pedis 'foot') are predatory arthropods belonging to the class Chilopoda of the subphylum Myriapoda, an arthropod group which includes millipedes and other multi-legged animals.
This small, lean, mostly nocturnal mammal native to tropical Asia and Africa is often called a 'cat' in its common nickname, despite not actually being a cat at all — what is it?
Civet is a small, lean, mostly nocturnal mammal native to tropical Asia and Africa, especially the tropical forests.

Forming colonies of thousands of genetically identical, sac-like polyps, these marine invertebrates secrete calcium carbonate to build the hard skeletons behind the world's tropical reefs — name them?
Coral are colonial marine invertebrates within the subphylum Anthozoa of the phylum Cnidaria.

This American nuclear physicist worked on the Manhattan Project and later led the Federation of American Scientists, best remembered for his 1959 testimony that helped sink a controversial cabinet nomination — who is he?
David L. Hill (November 11, 1919 - December 14, 2008) was an American nuclear physicist who worked on the Manhattan Project during World War II and was head of the Federation of American Scientists.
This waterfowl belongs to the same family as swans and geese, but is generally smaller and shorter-necked — and despite the shared family, swans and geese don't count as one. What is it?
Duck is the common name for numerous species of waterfowl in the family Anatidae.
This Italian-American physicist won the 1938 Nobel Prize, built the world's first artificial nuclear reactor (Chicago Pile-1), and is called the "architect of the nuclear age" — who was he?

Enrico Fermi (29 September 1901 - 28 November 1954) was an Italian-American physicist, renowned for being the creator of the world's first artificial nuclear reactor, the Chicago Pile-1, and a member of the Manhattan Project.
Immature at birth but developed by puberty, this network of organs includes the vagina, uterus, and fallopian tubes, protected by a fold called the labia majora — what's it called?
Female reproductive system is made up of the internal and external sex organs that function in the reproduction of new offspring.

Heterotrophs like animals, members of this kingdom eat by secreting enzymes into their surroundings, and they get around mainly by simply growing — except for the occasional flagellated spore drifting through air or water. What group is it?
Fungus (pl.: fungi or funguses) is any member of the group of eukaryotic organisms that includes yeasts, molds, as well as mushrooms.
One of the most widely distributed eagles in the Northern Hemisphere, this raptor is dark brown with lighter plumage on its nape and white markings on immature birds — which bird of prey?
Golden eagle (Aquila chrysaetos) is a bird of prey living in the Northern Hemisphere.
This daisy-family genus native to North America and Mexico includes the common sunflower and the Jerusalem artichoke among its roughly 50 species — which genus?
Helianthus is a genus comprising around 50 species of annual and perennial flowering plants in the daisy family Asteraceae commonly known as sunflowers.
With atomic number 1, this element's most common isotope holds just one proton and one electron, and it's what stars like the Sun mainly burn — what is it?
Hydrogen is a chemical element; it has the symbol H and atomic number 1.
Its name comes from the Ancient Greek for 'violet,' fitting for an element that boils into a violet gas — and it sits at atomic number 53 as the heaviest stable halogen. What is it?
Iodine is a chemical element; it has symbol I and atomic number 53.
Court astronomer and advisor to Elizabeth I, this mathematician and alchemist kept one of England's largest libraries and is credited with coining the phrase 'British Empire' — who was he?
John Dee (13 July 1527 - December 1608 or March 1609) was an English mathematician, astronomer, teacher, astrologer, occultist, and alchemist.
Despite being a kingfisher, this Australian bird rarely goes near water and can grow up to about 47 centimeters long — what is it?
Kookaburra are terrestrial tree kingfishers of the genus Dacelo native to Australia and New Guinea, which grow to between 28 and 47 cm (11 and 19 in) in length and weigh around 300 g (11 oz).

Named after the Italian word for lemon, this colorless liquid hydrocarbon is the main compound behind citrus peel fragrance, occurring mostly as a right-handed form extracted commercially by centrifugal separation or steam distillation - name the compound?

Limonene is a colorless liquid aliphatic hydrocarbon classified as a cyclic monoterpene, and is the major component in the fragrance and essential oil of citrus fruit peels, taking its name from Italian limone ("lemon").
This marsupial family native to Australia and New Guinea includes kangaroos, wallabies, quokkas, and tree-kangaroos among its 63 living species — what family is it?
Macropodidae is a family of marsupials that includes kangaroos, wallabies, tree-kangaroos, wallaroos, pademelons, the quokka, and several other groups.
This nitrogen-heavy compound forms durable plastic resins used in dry-erase boards and dinnerware, and its foam version scrubs stains as the innards of a Magic Eraser — name the chemical?
Melamine is an organic compound with the formula C3H6N6.
Its dust-like, fuzzy, colored appearance on food comes from spores, and its tubular branching network of hyphae counts as a single organism — what fungal structure is it?
Mold (US, PH) or mould (UK, CW) is one of the structures that certain fungi can form.
The paranasal sinuses all drain into this air-filled space that channels inhaled air from the nostrils down toward the throat — what is it?
Nasal cavity is an air-filled space above and behind the nose in the middle of the face.

Classified using a measurement of weight divided by the square of height, this medical condition is diagnosed when that figure exceeds 30 and is linked to cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes — what is it?
Obesity is a medical condition, considered a disease by multiple organizations, in which excess body fat has accumulated to such an extent that it can have negative effects on health.
Pair it with aspirin and caffeine and it's a first-line remedy for mild headaches; on its own it's the active ingredient many people know as acetaminophen — what is this over-the-counter drug?
Paracetamol is an analgesic and antipyretic agent used to treat fever and mild to moderate pain.
This inflammation of the back of the throat causes a sore throat and fever, most often from a viral infection, though strep bacteria cause roughly a quarter of cases in children — name the condition?
Pharyngitis is inflammation of the back of the throat, known as the pharynx.
Cough, chest pain, fever, and trouble breathing point to this infection of the lungs' alveoli, often classified by where it was caught — community or hospital — what is it?
Pneumonia is an inflammatory condition of the lung primarily affecting the small air sacs known as alveoli.
Belonging to the rose family, this flowering tree species gives us most plums, including the greengage and damson varieties — which species is it?
Prunus domestica is a species of flowering plant in the family Rosaceae.
With roughly 12,000 living species split across four classic orders — including the single-species tuatara branch — what ectothermic class is this?
Reptile are tetrapod vertebrate animals with an ectothermic metabolism and amniotic development.

Known from complete specimens found in Bolivia, this extinct armored jawless fish from the Ordovician period resembled a slender tadpole with eyes set like car headlamps on its oversized head — what is it?
Sacabambaspis is an extinct genus of armored jawless fish which lived in the Ordovician period.
Applied practically by Archimedes for the quadrature of a parabola, what do we call the addition of infinitely many terms, one after another, central to calculus?
Series (mathematics) is, roughly speaking, an addition of infinitely many terms, one after the other.
Known by such nicknames as 'sour dock' and 'spinach dock,' this tangy Eurasian herb thrives wild in grasslands and is often used as a leaf vegetable — which plant?
Sorrel (Rumex acetosa) is a perennial herbaceous plant in the family Polygonaceae.
The fifth most common element on Earth, this multivalent nonmetal usually turns up in sulfide and sulfate minerals and is a bright yellow crystalline solid — what is it?
Sulfur (American spelling or sulphur (Commonwealth spelling) is a chemical element; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.
A metabolite of caffeine processed in the liver, this bitter alkaloid is the main one in the cacao plant and turns up in chocolate, tea, and kola nuts. What is it?
Theobromine is the principal alkaloid of Theobroma cacao (cacao plant).
Caused by a single-celled parasite and often symptom-free, this common STI can be diagnosed by examining vaginal fluid under a microscope or with a DNA test — what is it?
Trichomoniasis (trich) is an infectious disease caused by the parasite Trichomonas vaginalis.
This broad category of creative disciplines spans painting, sculpture, photography, and architecture, and includes applied fields like industrial and fashion design — what do we call it?
Visual arts are art forms such as painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, photography, video, image, filmmaking, design, crafts, and architecture.
Known for a rapid side-to-side flight just before landing and living only in colonies, these black-and-yellow social wasps of the genera Vespula and Dolichovespula go by what North American name?
Yellowjacket is the common name in North America for predatory social wasps of the genera Vespula and Dolichovespula.
A rapid rise-and-fall of voltage across a cell membrane, this "spike" depolarizes neighboring spots and is how neurons and muscle cells fire — what is this electrical event called?
Action potential: Neuron communication by electric impulses.
Beginning about six hours after someone dependent on drinking stops, this set of symptoms can include shaking, sweating, seizures, and life-threatening delirium -- what is it called?
Formed when hydrogen atoms in ammonia are swapped out for carbon-based groups, which class of nitrogen-containing organic compounds includes aniline as its simplest aromatic member?
Amine: Chemical compounds and groups containing nitrogen with a lone pair (:N)

A German pharmacist coined this pigment's name from the Greek for 'flower' and 'dark blue' in 1835 — it shifts red to purple to blue depending on pH and colors blueberries, black rice, and autumn leaves; what is it?
A notoriously toxic metalloid and pnictogen with atomic number 33, it's used in lead alloys for car batteries and ammunition and as a semiconductor dopant — which element is it?
Arsenic: Chemical element with atomic number 33 (As). It is a metalloid and one of the pnictogens, and therefore shares many properties with its group 15 neighbors phosphorus and antimony.
This slender projection of a nerve cell typically carries electrical impulses away from the cell body toward other neurons, muscles, or glands — what is it called?
Axon: Long projection on a neuron that conducts signals to other neurons.
Named after the aromatic resin from which it was first derived, this simplest aromatic carboxylic compound forms salts widely used as food preservatives — what is it called?
This crested songbird in the crow family sports a black, U-shaped collar and is known for hiding acorns to eat later — which eastern North American bird?
Blue jay: Species of bird. The blue jay (Cyanocitta cristata) is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae, native to eastern North America.

Unique among mammals, human females are the only ones to permanently develop this secondary sex organ at puberty rather than just during pregnancy, and it later produces milk via the mammary gland — which body part?
Breast: Part of the female primate torso that has mammary glands.
With the formula CaC2, this industrial compound reacts with trace moisture to give off a garlicky smell and is used to generate acetylene gas in old-fashioned lamps — what is it?
Calcium carbide: Chemical compound. Its main use industrially is in the production of acetylene and calcium cyanamide.
This mammalian order of flesh-eating species is split into cat-like and dog-like suborders, Feliformia and Caniformia, and ranks as the sixth-largest order of mammals — which order?
Carnivora: Order of mammals. Carnivora ( kar-NIV-ər-ə) is an order of placental mammals specialised primarily in eating flesh, whose members are formally referred to as carnivorans.
Known in North America as fireweed and in Britain as rosebay willowherb, this perennial flowering plant thrives across the boreal forests of the Northern Hemisphere — which plant?
Chamaenerion angustifolium: Species of flowering plant in the willowherb family.
This fluoroquinolone antibiotic treats everything from typhoid fever to urinary tract infections but can rarely cause tendon rupture — what drug?
Ciprofloxacin: Fluoroquinolone antibiotic. Ciprofloxacin, sold under the brand name Cipro among others, is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic used to treat a number of bacterial infections.

Nicknamed 'flying lemurs' despite not being lemurs at all, these Southeast Asian gliding mammals are primates' closest living relatives and belong to an order whose name means 'skin wing' — what are they called?
First appearing in English in 1656 and later formalized in Latin by philosopher Christian Wolff, this field of study addresses the nature and origin of the universe — what field is it?
Cosmology: Study of the universe. Cosmology (from Ancient Greek κόσμος (cosmos) 'the universe, the world' and -λογία (logia) 'study of') is the study of the nature of the universe, the cosmos.
This biological process lets a cell make an exact copy of its genetic material by using each strand of the double helix as a template for a new one — what is it called?
DNA replication: Biological process. DNA replication ensures that each of the newly divided daughter cells receives its own copy of each DNA molecule.
A volatile, colorless liquid with a sweet, chloroform-like smell, this organochlorine (formula CH2Cl2) is slightly polar, won't mix with water, and is prized as a widely-used solvent. What is it?
Marketed as Cymbalta, this serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor treats depression, anxiety, and fibromyalgia pain — what is it?
This genus of deciduous trees, once popular as ornamental street trees across Europe and North America, was decimated by a fungal disease spread by bark beetles — which tree?
Elm: Flowering, deciduous trees, family Ulmaceae.

Defined by a single oxygen atom bridging two organyl groups (R−O−R′), this class of organic compounds includes a once-standard surgical anesthetic that lends its common one-word name to the whole family. What class of compound is this?
Ether: Organic compounds made of alkyl/aryl groups bound to oxygen (R–O–R')
Nicknamed the "Warthog" and flying since 1977, this straight-winged, twin-turbofan attack jet is the only U.S. production aircraft built solely for close air support against tanks — what is it?

Fairchild Republic A-10 Thunderbolt II: American close air support attack aircraft. In service since 1977, it is named after the Republic P-47 Thunderbolt strike-fighter of World War II, but is commonly referred to as the "Warthog".
Grown for both food and fiber, this plant's seeds are pressed into linseed oil while its stem fibers are woven into linen for sheets and clothing. What plant is it?
Found in the rainforests and savannas of sub-Saharan Africa, this snake has the longest fangs of any venomous species — up to two inches — and the highest venom yield of any snake — which snake?
Gaboon viper: Species of snake. It is the largest member of the genus Bitis.
The only venomous lizard native to the United States, this sluggish reptile from the Southwest rarely poses a real threat despite its fearsome reputation — what is it?
Gila monster: Largest species of lizard in the United States.

Despite its name, this marine reptile's shell ranges from olive to black — its nickname actually comes from the color of the fat beneath its carapace, built up from an all-plant diet — which species is this?
Green sea turtle: Species of large sea reptile. The dorsoventrally flattened body of C. mydas is covered by a large, teardrop-shaped carapace; it has a pair of large, paddle-like flippers.

Made by fusing heavy nuclei in tiny quantities, this superheavy element 108 has a special isotope whose "magic numbers" of protons and neutrons make its deformed nucleus unusually stable — what is it?
Hassium: Chemical element with atomic number 108 (Hs)
Hardy enough to survive winters as cold as -43°C, this shrub genus's aggressive roots fight soil erosion, and its berries and leaves are turned into food and skincare products — which genus?
Hippophae: Genus of flowering plants including sea buckthorn.
This huge insect order includes sawflies, wasps, bees, and ants, and its females often carry an egg-laying tube that doubles as a stinger — what order is it?
Hymenoptera: Order of insects. Over 150,000 living species of Hymenoptera have been described, in addition to over 2,000 extinct ones.
Fever, sore throat, body aches and fatigue that start one to four days after exposure and may spiral into pneumonia — there are four types of this viral infection. What is it?

Alongside Francis Crick, which American biologist co-proposed the double-helix structure of DNA in a 1953 Nature paper, building on the work of Rosalind Franklin, earning a share of the 1962 Nobel Prize?
This French mathematician ranged across number theory, complex analysis, and mathematical physics — and a crater on the Moon is named after him; who was he?
Often miscalled a 'bear,' this tailless, fluffy-eared Australian marsupial is actually a close cousin of the wombat — what is it?
Koala: Arboreal herbivorous marsupial native to Australia.

One of the five big cats in the genus Panthera, this slender, muscular predator wears dark spots clustered into rosettes and is split today into eight recognised subspecies across Africa and Asia — what is it?
Leopard: Species of cat native to Africa and Asia.

A four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft, this American plane is a comprehensive update of an older transport design, with over 500 delivered to 26 operators worldwide as of 2022. What aircraft is this?
Lockheed Martin C-130J Super Hercules: Military transport aircraft. The C-130J is a comprehensive update of the Lockheed C-130 Hercules, with new engines, flight deck, and other systems.
This is the common name for the larva of flies like houseflies and blowflies — though, confusingly, not for baby mosquitoes — what is it called?
This biological term covers the pairing of organisms for sexual reproduction, encompassing everything from copulation to external fertilization in fish and amphibians — what is it?
Mating: Process of pairing in biology.
Sold under the brand name Dolophine, this synthetic opioid is used to manage chronic pain and treat opioid use disorder by relieving cravings and withdrawal. What is it?
Methadone: Opioid analgesic and maintenance therapy.

Also called 'selective sound sensitivity syndrome,' this disorder causes specific sounds to trigger strong negative emotional and physiological reactions, though it isn't yet listed in the DSM-5-TR — what is it called?
Misophonia: Disorder of decreased tolerance to specific sounds.

Grouping over 30 inherited disorders that cause progressive weakening and wasting of skeletal tissue — with the Duchenne form affecting roughly half of all cases in young boys — what's this disease group called?
Muscular dystrophy: Diseases in which skeletal and visceral muscles break down over time.

First arising in wormlike organisms 550 to 600 million years ago, this body-wide network splits into a central hub of brain and spinal cord and a peripheral web of nerve fibers relaying signals to and from every body part — which network?
Nervous system: Part of an animal that coordinates actions and senses.
This burrowing, semiaquatic South American rodent munches river-plant stems and was shipped worldwide by fur farmers, only to become a destructive invasive pest — which animal is it?
Nutria: Semi-aquatic rodent from South America.
Farmed largely around a South African town, this flightless bird is the heaviest bird alive and can sprint 70 km/h — the fastest of any bird on land. What is it?
Ostrich: Genus of largest living birds.
This American physician-turned-clown founded the Gesundheit Institute in 1989 and travels the world dressing up to bring humor to hospital patients — who is he?

Positioned behind the mouth and nasal cavity, this throat structure channels food toward the esophagus and air toward the larynx, with a flap of cartilage guarding against the two crossing paths — what is it?
Pharynx: Part of the throat that is behind the mouth and nasal cavity.

Derived in 1900 by a German physicist who proposed that an oscillator's energy could only change in discrete increments, this principle describes the spectral density of radiation from a black body at a given temperature — what is it called?
Planck's law: Spectral density of light emitted by a black body.
This common name describes small aquatic crustaceans with an exoskeleton and ten legs, especially popular in the UK and Commonwealth nations for larger swimming decapods — what is it?
Prawn: Common name applied to some types of crustaceans.
This seabird's large, colorful beak fades after breeding season, and its short wings beat up to 400 times a minute to keep it airborne — what bird is it?
Domesticated roughly 8,000 years ago, this Southeast Asian bird species is the primary wild ancestor of today's chickens — which bird?
Red junglefowl: Species of bird; ancestor of the chicken. The red junglefowl was the primary species to give rise to today's many breeds of chicken (G. g. domesticus).
Nicknamed the 'Bone,' this variable-sweep-wing heavy bomber was dreamed up to fuse the B-58's Mach 2 speed with the B-52's range and payload — which aircraft is it?
Rockwell B-1 Lancer: American strategic bomber.
This business magnate founded the world's largest retailer by revenue in 1962, was the richest person in America throughout the 1980s, and left behind the country's wealthiest family — who is he?

Triggered when the body's own dysregulated response to infection starts damaging its tissues and organs, this life-threatening condition brings fever, rapid heartbeat, and confusion — which condition?

Sepsis: Life-threatening response to infection. Sepsis is a potentially life-threatening condition that arises when the body's dysregulated response to infection causes injury to its own tissues and organs.

This informal name applies to any shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc — a body plan that evolved independently many times through convergent evolution across unrelated lineages. What creature is it?
Slug: Shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc. Slug or land slug is a common name for any apparently shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc.
Prized as the standard soundboard material for stringed instruments, this coniferous genus has four-sided needles and dominates boreal forests across the Northern Hemisphere — which tree genus?
Spruce: Genus of coniferous evergreen trees.
This tangy reddish spice, made from a shrub in the cashew family, is a staple of Arab cuisine and holds symbolic significance on the Haft-sin table at Persian New Year — what is it?
Sumac: Related species of plants in the family Anacardiaceae.
Predicted by Mendeleev decades before its discovery and sitting in the periodic table between manganese and rhenium, what is the lightest element whose isotopes are all radioactive?
Technetium: Chemical element with atomic number 43 (Tc)
Tucked behind the breastbone and in front of the heart, this two-lobed organ is where immature T cells mature, and it's most active before adolescence — which organ?
Its name translates to 'three-horned face,' and this frilled dinosaur roamed present-day western North America right up until the asteroid strike 66 million years ago — what dinosaur is it?
Triceratops: Genus of Late Cretaceous dinosaur.
Also known by the common names bilberry, blaeberry, and whortleberry, this holarctic shrub produces edible blue fruit — what is it?
Neither bee nor ant despite being closely related, yellowjackets and hornets belong to this narrow-waisted insect group that can deliver a painful sting — what is it?
Wasp: Group of insects. Unlike true parasites, the wasp larvae eventually kill their hosts.
This Greek economist served as Finance Minister under Alexis Tsipras during the 2015 debt crisis, becoming internationally known for battling EU-imposed austerity — who is he?
Yanis Varoufakis: Greek economist and politician (born 1961)

The symbol for mendelevium is Md. Mendelevium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Md and atomic number 101.
What is the chemical symbol for ytterbium?
The symbol for ytterbium is Yb. Ytterbium is a chemical element; it has symbol Yb and atomic number 70.
